title: Psychotropic-induced weight gain
markers: Text in [verify] still needs checking against the source. Remove the tag once checked.
keyPoints: Weight gain is fastest in the **first 4–12 weeks**. A **≥5% gain in the first month** predicts substantial long-term gain, so act early.
**H1 + 5-HT2C blockade** is the strongest receptor predictor. Clozapine, olanzapine and mirtazapine block both.
**Metformin** has the strongest evidence for prevention and treatment. Start it alongside clozapine or olanzapine.
**Monitor everyone:** weight, waist, BP, glucose/HbA1c and lipids, at baseline and on a fixed schedule.

clinicalFeatures.definition: Clinically significant weight gain is a rise of **≥7% from baseline body weight**, the threshold used in CATIE and CAFE.

course.onset: Steepest in **weeks 4–12**; can continue for a year or more
course.doseRelated: Weakly; drug choice matters more than dose [verify]
course.reversible: Partly, after switching or adding treatment

clinicalFeatures.consequences: Metabolic syndrome, type 2 diabetes, dyslipidaemia, fatty liver disease and cardiovascular disease. Also harms self-image and is a leading reason patients stop medication.

bodySize.asian: ≥27.5 kg/m² (WHO Asian action point); ≥25 in Indian consensus [verify]
South Asian ≥90 cm men / ≥80 cm women

riskFactors: First episode, or little or no previous antipsychotic exposure
Low baseline BMI (more room to gain)
Rapid early gain: ≥5% in the first month
Personal or family history of obesity, diabetes or cardiovascular disease
Using a high-risk drug, or combining several weight-promoting drugs

drugsImplicated.notInLibrary: Also relevant but not yet in the library: TCAs (amitriptyline, doxepin, imipramine) and phenelzine (high); valproate (high); lithium and zotepine (moderate); lamotrigine (neutral); topiramate and zonisamide (weight loss).

notes: *The 2004 consensus specifies fasting glucose. HbA1c is now commonly used alongside or instead, but it is not part of the original schedule.
Lipids: the consensus says every 5 years if normal. Many services check annually.
Check glucose and lipids at 12 weeks even if weight is stable. Metabolic change can start before weight changes.

items: Diet, exercise and behavioural support from the start of treatment.
Review the whole regimen for weight-promoting drugs.
Move to a lower-risk agent: **aripiprazole, ziprasidone, lurasidone**, or **bupropion** for depression.

Weigh the risk of relapse. In CAMP, switching to aripiprazole led to more weight loss but **more patients stopped treatment** than in the stay group. For patients stable on clozapine, switching is rarely right.
**Adjunctive aripiprazole** (5–15 mg/day) added to clozapine produces modest weight loss.

**When to start (Carolan 2024 guideline):** with any high-risk antipsychotic (olanzapine, clozapine); with a medium-risk antipsychotic (quetiapine, risperidone, paliperidone) if the patient has a cardiometabolic risk factor, is **aged 10–25**, or has BMI 25–30; and with **any** antipsychotic if weight rises **>3% in the first year**.

metformin.titrationNote: Extended-release tablets taken with food reduce nausea and diarrhoea.
safety: **eGFR 30–45:** US label: do not start. UK label: start at a reduced dose, maximum 1000 mg/day, and review. **eGFR 45–59:** UK maximum 2000 mg/day.
Check **vitamin B12** periodically on long-term treatment.
Avoid in **harmful or excessive alcohol use** and in conditions that predispose to lactic acidosis.
**Children and adolescents:** metformin is licensed for type 2 diabetes from age 10. Dose per local paediatric guidance. [verify]
metformin.effect: Starting metformin with the antipsychotic reduced weight gain by about **4 kg** versus control. In established gain, mean loss was about **3.3 kg** versus placebo, with improved insulin resistance.

otherOptions.notes: **Liraglutide** (up to 3 mg/day): −5.3 kg versus placebo in clozapine- or olanzapine-treated patients (RCT). Evidence for **semaglutide** is growing. Watch for GI effects.
ENLIGHTEN-2: **17.8% vs 29.8%** gained ≥10% body weight at 24 weeks, versus olanzapine alone. Contraindicated with opioids. Not available in all regions.
50–200 mg/day. Reduces weight; cognitive slowing and paraesthesia limit use.
Licensed for obesity; little data specifically in drug-induced weight gain.
Weak evidence in this population. GI side effects limit adherence.

2022 ASMBS/IFSO: recommended at **BMI ≥35**; consider at **30–34.9** with metabolic disease. Asian populations: lower thresholds, with surgery offered from **BMI ≥27.5**. [verify] Psychiatric illness does not exclude referral. Re-check lithium levels and other drug dosing afterwards, because absorption changes.

mechanism.effect: Less satiety, more appetite, sedation and less activity. Activates hypothalamic AMPK. Strongest single receptor predictor.
Loss of serotonergic appetite suppression, so more food intake.
Largest effect: **clozapine, olanzapine, mirtazapine**. Quetiapine acts mainly through H1 (weak 5-HT2C blockade).

mechanism.mechanism: Less POMC/α-MSH → MC4R signalling; relative dominance of NPY/AgRP
Rising leptin with central leptin resistance
Direct effects on insulin sensitivity in muscle, liver and fat
mechanism.effect: Insulin resistance and raised triglycerides, **sometimes before weight gain**. Rare early DKA or HHS reported with clozapine and olanzapine.
Altered energy harvest. Evidence is mostly preclinical.

differentialDiagnosis: **Fluid retention or oedema** rather than fat gain.
**Recovery of appetite** as depression or psychosis improves.

keyEvidence.finding: People with severe mental illness die **10–20 years earlier**, largely from cardiometabolic disease. Obesity affects about **45–55%** of people with schizophrenia, 1.5–2 times the general-population rate.
Mean gain at **10 weeks**: clozapine ~4.5 kg, olanzapine ~4.2 kg, risperidone ~2.1 kg, haloperidol ~1.1 kg, ziprasidone ~0.04 kg.
**30% on olanzapine** gained ≥7% of body weight during the trial (up to 18 months), versus 7–16% on the other drugs.
Early psychosis: ≥7% gain at 52 weeks in **80% (olanzapine), 58% (risperidone), 50% (quetiapine)**.
Switching to aripiprazole: more weight loss than staying, but more treatment discontinuation.
Network meta-analyses ranking antipsychotics on weight and metabolic effects.

examPearls: Clinically significant weight gain = **≥7% of baseline weight**.
**H1 + 5-HT2C** blockade predicts weight gain: clozapine, olanzapine, mirtazapine.
**Bupropion** is the only antidepressant consistently linked to weight loss.
**Samidorphan** is an opioid antagonist, so olanzapine-samidorphan is contraindicated with opioids.
Cholinesterase inhibitors and stimulants tend to cause **weight loss**, not gain.
Metabolic changes (insulin resistance, triglycerides) can appear **before** weight gain.

selfTest.question: A 22-year-old starts olanzapine 10 mg for first-episode psychosis. Four weeks later they have gained 6% of baseline weight. What is the best next step?

options.text: Recheck at 12 weeks; early gain usually settles
Lifestyle support and start metformin; consider a lower-risk antipsychotic

selfTest.explanation: A ≥5% gain in the first month predicts substantial long-term gain, and the patient is young and on a high-risk drug. The 2024 guideline supports metformin here, alongside lifestyle support and a review of whether a lower-risk antipsychotic is suitable.
